see.n: Armenian Church of the Holy Resurrection
see.pr: Free, but tipping the caretaker is a friendly gesture
see.b: A small, cosy church built in 1781 by Armenian missionaries. Mass is conducted only a few times throughout the year, usually during Christmas and Good Friday. Tours are informal, and could be organised by the caretaker, Mr Martin.
Anglican church built in 1821.
A mosque in Old Dhaka that dates from the 17th century, most likely built by the Mughals.
Built in the early 18th century, it has since been redecorated with hundreds of tiles with star patterns. Tourists are welcome to visit outside of prayer times.
National Temple of Bangladesh, built in the 12th century, dedicated to the Goddess Durga and God Shiva. It is the seat of Bangladesh's Hindu priesthood.
Built during the 17th century by the Mughals as a house for the imam, a religious leader. Its architecture possesses a mix of Mughal and British influences.
A mosque built during the 15th century; it is characterised by its seven white domes that peek upwards from the structure.

Built in 1640 the Dhanmondi Eidgah, is the oldest surviving Mughal monument in Dhaka. It was used for Eid prayers for both Eid ul Fitr and Eid ul Zoha. The Eidgah consists of an open courtyard measuring 45 m by 40 m, and is surrounded…

A well-preserved historic mosque on Lalbagh Road. It lies on a raised platform with a stairway on the east, an arched gateway and a central doorway. Persian inscriptions on its arch and Mihrab speak of its construction in 1705.
An ornate early 19th-century mosque in the Armenian quarter decorated with blue star-motifs.

It is the oldest surviving mosque in Dhaka, dating back to the Sultanate of Bengal. It was built in 1454 by Bakht Binat in the reign of Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah. It is beside the Hayat Bepari Bridge in the Narinda area.
It was built by Murshid Quli Khan, the last Mughal governor and first Nawab of Bengal.

see.pr: Foreigners: Tk 75, under-12s: Tk 2, locals and SAARC citizens: Tk 5, disabled pe
see.b: A British Raj-era building that served as a residence for the Nawab of Dhaka. It lies on the banks of the Buriganga River, and is famous for its pink stonework. There are 31 rooms within, and the huge dome on top can be seen from miles…

see.pr: There are separate fees for locals and tourists; both are fairly cheap
see.b: Built in 1678 AD by Prince Mohammad Azam, son of Mughal emperor Aurangazeb. The fort was the scene of many bloody battles, including those during the Mughal era, a revolt against the British during the time of the Raj and protection for…

Former residence of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. It has been transformed into a museum and contains a rare collection of personal effects and photographs of his life and times. He was assassinated in 1975…

The Katras were the caravansaries of the city under Mughal rule. The most prominent were the palatial Bara Katra (Great Caravansary) and the smaller Choto Katra (Young Caravansary). Built in 1643 and 1663 respectively, they hosted…

A unique creation of the late Narendra Narayan Roy, the landlord of Baldha. Established in 1904, the garden with its rich collection of indigenous and exotic plants is one of the most exciting attractions for botanists, naturalists and…

In the late nineteenth century Bahadur Shah Park was the centre of Dhaka with European style architecture with several civic and religious buildings and educational institutions around it. It was here that the revolting sepoys and their…
A huge river port on the banks of the Buriganga River. Catch a ride on a boat here and cruise along the river, soaking in the surrounding chaos and sites.
A nature park/getaway of sorts with ponds, boat rides, along with a library and mosque.

see.n: Dharmarajika Buddhist Monastery Complex (Kamalapur Buddhist Monastery)
see.b: A Buddhist temple and monastery established in 1960, with a number of other facilities on site. There are various mosaics, murals, statues and artefacts at the monastery.

It is a water body adjacent to Sectors 10, 9, 7, and 3 in West Uttara. Such a natural feature within an urban setting enhances the beauty of Uttara. However, due to encroachment and pollution, much of its beauty has faded. Nowadays, the…

Located beside Uttara High School and College, this is a large and beautiful park. It is an ideal place to sit and breathe amidst nature. Note that it has specific visiting hours which may change from time to time.

see.n: Dhaka Metro Rail Exhibition and Information Center
see.b: This center was established to inform and raise awareness about the Dhaka Metro Rail. Alongside the metro rail experience, visitors can learn about its history through galleries. You can also purchase model metro trains here, which are…

This is a residential area developed by RAJUK. Here the tall buildings stand out in the flat landscape and attract visitors. The natural environment also fascinates people. Many come here to see the blooming Kans grass. At the entrance…
This lake stretches from the Khalpar of Sector 12 through Sectors 15 and 17 up to Mirpur DOHS. Its rural environment makes it one of the most popular attractions in Uttara.

This is an area located in Sector 17. To its south are official buildings of various universities and institutions. Many visitors come to see these aesthetic buildings in a semi-rural setting. The area also has several restaurants.
Established in 2023, this Hindu temple is not very ornate, but it is beautifully decorated during festivals. Those occasions are the best time to visit.
Located very close to Mirpur DOHS, this area is popular for its Kans grass fields.
The only cultural venue in Uttara. On various special occasions, concerts, street plays, and cultural programs are organized here.
This is an amusement park. Though small in size, it is not a bad place to spend some leisure time. It also has a cinema hall, and if you buy a ticket for the hall, entry to the park is free.
A resort located in the Diabari for leisure. Some wild animals are kept here for display.
The only place in Diabari Lake for kayaking.
The only government hospital in Uttara.

see.n: Uttara Adhunik Medical College and Hospital
see.b: Also known as Bangladesh Medical College and Hospital, it is the largest hospital in the area.

see.n: Shaheed Monsur Ali Medical College Hospital

see.b: Covering of land at Mirpur, the Gardens are a haven of peace in the chaos of the city. It is next to the zoo, so both can be visited in one trip.

see.pr: Tk 10; 0-2 years, school and University students are free with ID
see.b: Colourful and attractive collections of different local and foreign species of animals and birds, including the majestic Royal Bengal Tiger. Elephant and horse riding is available for a very cheap Tk 5 and Tk 3 respectively.

The national war memorial is located on the outskirts of Dhaka in Savar. It is a modernist monument with gardens and lakes where the national flower water lily often blooms. The memorial grounds offer a peaceful getaway from frenetic…
This is the national cricket stadium, capacity 25,400; the name means "Tiger of Bengal". It also hosts Dhaka Dominators in the Bangladesh Premier League, a T20 cricket tournament.
The national mosque of Bangladesh. It was built in 1968, and is the 10th largest mosque in the world.
Official residence of the President. This grand palace of the British India era is only visible from the outside.

see.a: 27 R K Mission Road, Gopibag, Dhaka
see.b: A Hindu temple and complex that was founded in 1916. The architecture is Indian-influenced.

see.pr: Foreigners: Tk 75, locals and SAARC citizens: Tk 10, disabled persons: free
see.b: Contains a large number of interesting collections, including sculptures and paintings from the Hindu, Buddhist and Muslim periods. Next door is a popular public library.

A leading private museum which documents the liberation struggle of Bangladesh from Pakistan in 1971, including the 1971 Bangladesh Genocide and the political and armed resistance movement of the Bangladeshi people

Located west of Shahidullah Hall at Dhaka University, this historical mosque was built to honour the former ruler of the region. The inscriptions on the mosque seem to state that it was built in 1484 CE, but was repaired heavily in 1700 CE.
A memorial of the Greeks of Dhaka built somewhere in the early 1900s.
It was built as the residence of the British Governor, it illustrates a happy blend of European and Mughal architecture. Now houses the Supreme Court.
An architecturally beautiful building named after Lord Curzon. Once intended as a town hall, it now houses the Science Faculty of the University of Dhaka.
Built in 1830, it is the largest Sikh temple in Bangladesh and commemorates the visit of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, to Bengal in the 14th century.

see.a: University of Dhaka, in front of the Faculty of Arts
see.b: A statue dedicated to those who died in the 1971 Liberation War. Designed by sculptor Abdullah Khaled it is built of reinforced concrete and reaches a height of . It was inaugurated on 16 December 1979. The sculpture consists of three…

see.a: In front of the Dhaka Medical College, University of Dhaka
see.b: A symbol of Bengali nationalism. This monument was built to commemorate the martyrs of the historic language movement of 1952. Thousands of people with floral wreaths and bouquets gather on 21 February annually, paying respect to the…
Revolutionary poet Kazi Nazrul Islam died on the 29 August 1976 and was buried here.

A race course of the British times, it has been converted into a park. It was the place where independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Raman delivered a historic oath of independence speech before the 1971 War, and where the Pakistani army…

It is one of the largest parks in Dhaka, seen as the city's equivalent to Kolkata's Maidan and New York City's Central Park. This huge sprawling area was the site of Mughal gardens and tombs before becoming a public park and race course…

At the spot where Sheikh Mujibur Raman delivered a historic oath of independence speech before the 1971 War, and where the Pakistani army surrendered a few months later. The museum consists of a 50-m-high glass tower of light. The…
The eternal flame was inaugurated by Prime Minister Sheik Hasina on 7 Mrach 1997. The flame burns eternally at the Northern end of Suhrawardi Uddyan, beneath the Bangladesh National flag.

see.n: Mausoleum of Three Leaders (তিন নেতার মাজার)
see.b: Eternal resting place of great national leaders, Sher-e-Bangla A.K. Fazlul Haque, Hossain Shahid Suhrawardy and Khaja Nazimuddin. All the three men served as Prime Minister of Bengal in British India.

see.a: Suhrawardy Uddyan, behind Mausoleum of Three Leaders
see.b: This mosque and tomb, constructed in 1679 by Haji khwaja Shahbaz, a rich merchant of Dhaka.
A thousand-year-old temple, dedicated to the goddess Kali. The temple was vandalized during the Pakistan war of 1971 and later reconstructed.

see.pr: Tk 500 for advanced bookings, Tk 600 for on arrival visits
see.b: Designed by the famous American architect, Louis I. Kahn, it is renowned as a modern architectural wonder of the region. The Parliament is surrounded by gardens that form a peaceful getaway from the chaos of the city. The building is…

see.n: National Museum of Science and Technology
see.b: A museum and modern learning centre displaying the latest scientific discoveries. Each weekend, a starwatching evening is held for Tk 10.
Representative Bangladesh air force planes and history on display.
An old Portuguese-influenced church built in 1677. The façade has been repainted into heavy Indian-style colours. A large, new building has been built next door to allow a larger congregation.

see.h: Thu-Tue; closed Wed. Shows start Fri 10:00 to 18:30; other days 10:30 to 16:30
see.pr: Tk 50 for Planetarium; Tk 20 for Space Ride Simulator
see.b: A planetarium built on of land, its spaces range in size from its 21-metre dome, seating 275 people; to three-metre inflatable and portable domes where people sit on the floor. The Planetarium dome simulates Earth and its cool blue sky.…
A Buddhist monastery that was founded in 1981, and has been at its current site since 1989. It is popular with visiting Buddhist businessmen and foreign dignitaries.
A regional modernist transport system in central Dhaka with numerous bridges, flyovers and viaducts over a huge natural lake.
Houses a representative collection of folk-art, modern art and paintings by numerous artists of Bangladesh.

eat.b: Old Dhaka was famed for its lines of biryani restaurants. Some of the more famous outfits are still going and Hajjee Beryani is one of them. It revels in its eccentric reputation for opening only at certain times and only cooking a…

On the ground floor of the hotel is a large and popular restaurant, busy anytime of the day with Bangladeshi families and businessmen. Food is pretty darn good, if unpredictable in its timing. Sometimes you'll have a choice of chicken…
Does fantastic biryani and goat leg roast.
High-end Chinese restaurant
Kebab and Mughlai food. Mouth-watering and unbelievably tasty.
Very inexpensive local food, famous for Kacchi Biryani and kebabs. A meal for one can run you Tk 50-300.
Famous for its beef and mutton kebab. Different from the other Star Hotel listed here also.

eat.n: Sea Shell Restaurant and Party Palace
eat.b: A Chinese and Thai restaurant, known for its good quality food.
An Arabian fast-food chain.
An Indian restaurant where you can get almost all types of Indian cuisine.
A nice place for coffee and light fast food in a pleasant environment.
Along with biryani, you can have a full meal here at a moderate cost.
Famous for its kebabs.
Offers various oven-baked pizzas at a moderate price.
A bakery and sweet shop. Fast food is also available.
A pastry and fast-food shop. Food prices here are very low.

A burger, fries and rootbeer float will cost nearly BDT300, which seems to be no problem for the well-off young Bangladeshi teens that fill the tables. The jukebox filled with Backstreet Boys may either add or detract from the experience.
A Chinese/Thai restaurant that prides itself in offering 'authentic' cuisine, and this is backed up by the number of Chinese expats seen eating there on any given night.

eat.a: House 10, Road 53, near Gulshan North Avenue
eat.pr: Food items Tk 200-300, Cupcakes around Tk 160
eat.b: Famous for the cupcakes, the milk shakes, the cheesecake and other pastries. A wide range of sandwiches and other dishes are also available. Free WLAN is also available.

eat.a: House 66, Ground Floor, Road No 9, Block F, Banani
eat.b: Offers different coffee specialities made from imported beans as well as exotic drinks like Lemogini, Shikanjee, Guava Frappe, Mango Yogurt & Mandolito. CoFi 11 has a beautiful terrace with nice view over Gulshan. They also have…
Decent Italian restaurant that delivers pizza and pasta. A meal costs Tk 400-600.
Serves steaks. Expect to pay at least Tk 2,000 per person for a three-course dinner.

Restaurant, swimming pool, and tennis courts. Although it was built primarily for the employees of the U.S. Embassy in Dhaka and their families, membership is generally available to other people as well.
Serves good local dishes for the budget traveler. Expect to pay Tk 150-200 for a 3 course meal. Although you can possibly get lunch/dinner for as low as Tk 60.
The top restaurant in the hotel serves very good seafood. Expect to pay Tk 3,000 for a 3-course meal with drinks. The hotel has other good restaurants too.
A fancy steakhouse and seafood restaurant in the InterContinental Hotel. Also has wine pairings.
A good but very expensive buffet with breakfast, lunch and dinner.
A lounge next to the pool in the InterContinental Hotel with things like sandwiches and salads. More affordable than the other restaurants in the hotel.
Biryani, kebabs, cakes, ice cream, biscuits, fruit, and also gifts.
Very famous for cakes and fast food.
A medium quality, old Chinese restaurant which serves Chinese and Thai food.
An upscale restaurant with a haunted theme (VOOT-meaning ghost in Bengali), high quality food, next to the well known Rifles Square Market.
A large food court in the Bashundhara City Mall with all manner of fast food, western food, Bangladeshi food and more. There is also a slightly higher end Food Hall in the food court.
The proprietor was employed in the restaurant business in Italy and this place serves fairly authentic thin-crust pizzas and pastas.
A Mexican restaurant serving burritos, enchiladas, quesadillas and others.

Korean restaurant near the Egyptian embassy. Table-top barbecue and most popular Korean dishes are available, along with a selection of sushi and sashimi. Popular with Koreans and other expats. Expect to pay at least Tk 500 per person…
Don't expect to be rubbing shoulders with any French ambassadors, however.

eat.a: 12 Abbas Garden, New Airport Road, Mohakhali
eat.b: is a duty-free shop that is only permitted to sell alcohol to passport-bearing foreigners or their drivers who bring their passports in when they purchase.

eat.a: Kha-47-1 Pragati Sarani, Shahzadpur, North Badda
eat.b: Definitely the best coffee in Dhaka. With foreign ownership, an on-site coffee-roasting machine and huge sacks of coffee in the back, this is definitely the place to get your caffeine fix. Prices reasonable. No meals yet, just muffins…
